resources.string: Transferred heat = arterial surplus × transfer share / 100, with the share entered as a percentage. Arterial surplus left = starting surplus minus transferred heat.

Near each testis in the scrotum, the testicular artery and the pampiniform veins of the spermatic cord carry blood in opposite directions. Heat can pass from warmer arterial blood to cooler venous blood without the blood mixing. In a two-arrow sketch, the artery points toward the testis and the veins point away; a cross-arrow shows heat transfer. The model simply moves a chosen share of a fictional arterial surplus into the venous tally. The arbitrary heat units (hu) and share are teaching inputs, not temperatures, measured exchange efficiencies, or fertility predictions.
